 Fantasy Share Fantasy Week 8 WR/CB Matchups For Fantasy Football: CeeDee Lamb, Parker Washington & More
 Chris Allen locks down the wide receiver/cornerback matchups to target and avoid for fantasy football in Week 8.
 Christopher Allen 2d ago Share Published Oct 30, 2026, 4:00 AM ET 
 A few weeks ago, I mentioned that my favorite part of poker isn’t the math. It’s reading the other players at the table. Vibes over stats, I always say. But there’s a catch I didn’t bring up. The longer the session goes, the more they’re reading me, too. My hand ranges, and bluffs form a pattern. I get my hand caught in the cookie jar at some point. So if I don’t change my approach, I’m the one getting picked apart.
 The NFL is hitting that point now. We’re getting some idea of each team’s offensive identity. Well, so do defensive coordinators. They’ve got seven weeks of film on every receiver, and they’re starting to take away what worked. The matchups that matter from here on out aren’t just about talent or volume. They’re about who adjusts first. So, let’s look at which receivers might have the upper hand to win the counter-punch in Week 8, and which ones might get caught bluffing.
 WR/CB Matchups to Target in Fantasy Football for Week 8 
 Week 7 Recap: Justin Jefferson (32), Jalen Coker (81). I probably could’ve done better if I had just picked WRs at random. Jefferson had a 26% target rate (season high with Kyler Murray ), and Coker’s 11% was a season low. I’m willing to give Jettas some grace because it was just his second full game with Murray. But the Panthers’ entire operation on offense requires a deeper look coming out of the bye, and some caution since they’re on a short week.  
 CeeDee Lamb vs. Cardinals 
 There’s a saying that goes something along the lines of elite talent exists at the intersection of talent and situation. CeeDee Lamb just capped off Week 7 with his third top-6 finish of the season , so there’s no question about the talent part. His usage backs up the sentiment.
 Per our UR game logs , Lamb is yet to play a full game without earning 20+% of Dak Prescott ’s targets. And with Prescott averaging the third-most dropbacks of any starter, Lamb’s target-earning skill is part of what makes him a high-end option every week. Plus, when you zoom out to his offensive situation, we can put another point in the “Lamb is elite” column.
 Team Pass Rate Over Expectation: +1.8%, 6th (among all teams)
 Green-Zone PROE: -1.2%, 13th
 QB Completion Percentage Over Expectation: +0.8%, 14th 
 Above-average marks across the board in terms of volume and quality of targets. Lamb specifically is tied for 19th in catchable target rate out of 59 qualifiers (min. 150 routes). More importantly, only Amon-Ra St. Brown and Matthew Golden have more targets when their teams get into scoring position. Finally, let’s take one more step back and factor in Lamb’s defensive matchup for Week 8.
 Yards per Game Allowed to WRs: 21st
 Explosive Play Rate Allowed: 29th
 PPR PPG Allowed: 15th 
 Four of the last five WR1s to face Arizona’s secondary have finished with double-digit PPR points. Two of them went nuclear ( Malik Nabers –23.2, Jaxon Smith-Njigba –42.5). With the Cardinals’ defensive front unable to generate pressure, Prescott and Lamb will be a top duo coming out of Week 8.
 Parker Washington vs. Colts 
 The Jaguars are coming off of their bye, so it’s been a couple of weeks since we’ve seen Parker Washington in action. Let’s recap where he left things.
 On the plus side, after a couple of weeks toward the middle of the passing totem pole, Washington was back on top in terms of target rate. He not only led Jacksonville’s WRs in share of looks from Trevor Lawrence , but air yards, too. But their connection was off, too.
 For all of the Texans’ problems on defense, the spine of their secondary and ability to limit interior receivers hasn’t been their weakest point. Along with a bump in Washington’s aDOT (up to 14.4 air yards), the added context of matchup and increased downfield usage makes his WR37 result understandable. Besides, had Washington broken a tackle in the red zone for a TD, there’d be no concern about a return to the top 12. But against the Colts, there shouldn’t be any anyway.
 Receptions Allowed per Slot Route: 24th
 Defensive EPA per Play (to Slot WRs): 20th
 Fantasy PPG Allowed: 22nd 
 The Colts had CB Justin Walley as their primary nickel corner coming into Week 7. Leading up to last Sunday, he was allowing the second-most yards per snap in coverage from the slot (min. 50 snaps). On Sunday, CB Cam Taylor-Britt took over, but he’s now on IR and Walley is nursing a knee injury. If there’s any place to pick on the Colts’ defense through the air, it’ll be to the inside, setting up Washington for a big day after his in-season break.
 Sneaky WR/CB Matchups for Fantasy Football in Week 8 
 Recap: Jaylin Noel (WR82), Denzel Boston (WR46), Courtland Sutton (WR40). I was playing with fire recommending a WR connected to Bo Nix (i.e., Sutton’s situation). That’s part of rolling the dice with “sneaky” matchups, but we’ll look for better environments moving forward. Noel got hurt early in the second half, but his routes and targets were down, as I noted as a concern. With Boston, at least he got the targets (26%), but Deshaun Watson just missed him on a long TD . He’ll be back on this list in the future. 
 DJ Moore vs. Ravens 
 Obviously, I’m assuming DJ Moore gets back on the field after missing two games and getting the bye to rest his shoulder. He’s still practicing in the red, no-contact jersey , but it’s Moore’s first limited session on a Wednesday since Week 4. I realize we only have two games with him active, but those should be enough to have him on our starting roster.
 Week 1: 27% (Target Share), 46% (Air Yard Share), 33% (3/4 Down Target Rate)
 Week 3: 38%, 52%, 56%
 I usually don’t mention how often a receiver earns a target in obvious passing situations. But it bears mentioning in Moore’s case as to how quickly he became a primary asset for Josh Allen . There was no ramp-up. No time for the two to get on the same page. They just were. Moore’s familiarity with HC Joe Brady likely helped. But immediately displacing the other receivers is noteworthy. So is facing the Ravens.
 Yards per Game Allowed (to WRs): 28th
 Passing Success Rate Allowed: 30th
 Fantasy PPG Allowed: 25th 
 From Chris Olave in Week 2 (22.6 PPR points) to both of my Bengals WRs (26.8 – Higgins, 17.2 – Chase), receivers attached to competent QBs have performed well against Baltimore’s coverage. Actually, take that back. Carnell Tate snuck in a 9-145-0 line, too. Anyway, with the defense keying on Allen’s legs, Moore should be able to take advantage of the secondary.
 Germie Bernard vs. Browns 
 Thinking back to my poker analogy in the intro. Yes, Sunday will be a divisional rematch between the Steelers and Browns. That’s where all of the “I-know-what-you-know-what-I-know” narratives come out. But Germie Bernard wasn’t a featured player in Week 4. Since then, let’s look at how the Browns have fared against WR1s.
 Week 5: Garrett Wilson, 11-104-1, 3.06 (YPRR)
 Week 6: Zay Flowers, 11-66-0, 1.94
 Week 7: Carnell Tate, 7-69-0, 2.23
 At first glance, these look like three different receivers. But a couple of notes here. First, Wilson and Tate ran more routes from the slot against the Browns than their average against any other team. Flowers already operates from the inside on 48% of his snaps, so not much change there for him. Second, in-breaking routes were the primary weapon. All three ran crossers or hitches on over 55% of their targets. Bernard’s already at a 42% in-breaking route rate in three games as a starter, with over half of his routes coming from the slot. If Pittsburgh wants to show Cleveland something new, Bernard is the key. 
 Tre Tucker at Jets
 Two things to put out about Tre Tucker (former Bearcat!) as an under-the-radar play.
 I flipped off the percentage (remember, percent  per cent  “of 100,” easy!) to show Tucker’s raw target totals each week to highlight Kirk Cousins isn’t just looking for him a few times a game. Since Week 4, Tucker (7.8 per game) is averaging more looks each week than Denzel Boston (6.8), Christian Watson (6.5) and Garrett Wilson (6.0). But the aDOT makes the Raiders’ (pseudo) WR1 volatile. However, the Jets make a play like him somewhat appealing.
 On intermediate throws, HC Aaron Glenn’s defense is giving up the seventh-highest passing success rate. Teams have thrown to their receivers at depths between 10 and 20 air yards. Half have turned into a first down or a score. But we know Tucker’s calling card: the big play . 
 Even there, the Jets have made their opposing QB right more often than not. They’re allowing a 51.9% completion rate on throws of 15 air yards or more (10th-highest). Brock Bowers is still the WR1 for Vegas. But if this game does turn into a shootout, expect Tucker to be a part of the fantasy festivities.
 WR/CB Matchup to Avoid in Week 8 
 Recap: Malik Nabers (WR15). Credit to OC Matt Nagy and J.J. McCarthy for an amazing game plan and execution against the Texans. McCarthy played his best football since joining the league, and Nabers turned in the second-most yards of any WR against Houston. Huge whiff on my part, and we’ll need to recalibrate our expectations against the Texans moving forward. 
 DK Metcalf vs. Browns 
 So if I talked about Bernard’s inside work as a boon, DK Metcalf stuck outside should serve as a warning. Yes, Aaron Rodgers and Metcalf stuck it to the Browns back in Week 4 (5-115-0 on 9 targets). Over a third came on a single play . Since then, I’d venture to say Cleveland learned how to limit receivers with a similar on-field deployment to Metcalf.
 Yards per Game Allowed (to Outside WRs): 10th
 Explosive Play Rate Allowed: 8th
 Defensive EPA per Play: 13th 
 Over the past three weeks, the Browns have allowed just four plays of more than 20 yards. And as I mentioned, perimeter receivers have had to slide to the interior or run in-breaking patterns to create separation. Neither of which is Metcalf’s specialty. There’s always a chance for Rodgers to connect with him on a deep pass. But expecting another top-24 result is tough to see in this AFC North rematch.
